item.description:
New Features

  • Split PDF. Drop a PDF in, type the page ranges you want — 1-3, 5, 8- — and each range becomes its own file saved next to the original. Leave it blank to split every page separately. Works in the app, from the command line (picmal-cli split-pdf), in Shortcuts, and in Raycast.

Bug Fixes

  • "Remove Metadata" in the Compress shortcut now actually strips metadata. The metadata step was running but couldn't read your settings, so it quietly did nothing. And if a file was already small enough that Picmal skipped compression, the original came back unmodified — GPS and all. Turn the option on and it's gone, same as Convert.

Bug Fixes

  • Opus conversions no longer fail at high bitrates. Setting the bitrate to 320 kbps would always error out because libopus tops out at 256 kbps. It now clamps to 256 kbps quietly instead of aborting.
  • Picmal no longer crashes when many files fail at once. In large batches on Intel Macs, rapid back-to-back failures could trigger a crash. A race condition in error reporting was the cause.
  • "Remove Metadata" in the Shortcuts action now actually strips metadata. The setting was passed in correctly but dropped before it reached the step that does the stripping, so GPS and EXIF stayed in the file no matter what you set.
  • iPhone Live Photos and other `.mov` files with bad timestamps no longer fail to convert. Some videos carry timestamps that confuse the video muxer part way through, aborting the conversion. Picmal now catches that and retries with the timestamps corrected.
  • Image conversions no longer crash when a process is killed mid-read. The code that captured output from image conversion processes could raise an unrecoverable error if interrupted during a large batch. It now uses the same safe reading approach the rest of the app already used.

Bug Fixes

  • The error detail popover no longer balloons to full screen. On wide displays, it could stretch to fill the window. It now wraps at 280 px.
  • Intel tool-launch failures no longer show as a misleading "path issue". An `` dynamic library error (common on Intel or under Rosetta) was being caught by an overly broad check and turned into a generic "path issue" message. The real error comes through now.
  • The file list no longer bleeds into the title bar. On macOS 15, rows could scroll up behind the traffic-light buttons. The title bar area now stays clean and matches the list.

Improvements

  • Container swaps are now near-instant. Changing a video's container while keeping the same codec (MOV to MP4, MP4 to MKV, and so on) now copies the stream directly instead of re-encoding it. Even with a video preset active, a 5-second clip finishes in well under a second instead of taking 20+.
  • Mixed image and video batches are faster. When images and videos process side by side, image jobs now leave a couple of CPU cores free for video encodes. Before, the image pool took everything and video conversions crawled.
  • Tighter PNG compression at Max Compression level. Level 9 now uses Zopfli on smaller files — a slower but stronger compressor that squeezes a few extra percent out without touching quality.
  • WebP tries harder on bigger files. Picmal already runs two encodes and keeps whichever comes out smaller. That now applies to files up to 10 MB, up from 4 MB.
  • AVIF is smaller at aggressive quality settings. Pick a low quality preset and the encoder works a bit harder, shaving a few percent off without touching quality.

Bug Fixes

  • Setting a target frame rate above the source no longer inflates the file. Picmal was duplicating frames to hit the target, making files bigger and encodes slower for no visual gain. The target now only applies when it actually lowers the rate — set 48 fps on a 25 fps clip and the output stays at 25.
  • The "Saving" estimate no longer shows in plain Convert mode. It was sample-encoding video behind the scenes even when no compression would happen, and showing a misleading saving percentage in the file list. It only runs in Compress mode or when "Compress after convert" is on.

Improvements

  • Unsupported formats now say "Not supported" instead of "Failed". Formats that can't be compressed (like RAW or DNG) used to land in the same red Failed state as a real processing error, complete with an error-info popover. They now show a plain red "Not supported" directly, so it's clear this is a format limitation, not something that went wrong.
  • Re-added output files now say "Skipped". If you dropped in a folder that already held compressed files from a previous run, those files got picked up as inputs and then quietly did nothing during compression, showing "Waiting" with no explanation. They now show "Skipped" with a tooltip explaining that another file in the batch is already writing to that name.
  • Schedule sheet is a little roomier. Wider and with more breathing room, so the subtitle text wraps less awkwardly.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed bottom-bar buttons invisible in light mode on macOS 26. The Clear, Again, Cancel, and Convert/Compress buttons all disappeared against the light toolbar. A transparent tint override was making the Liquid Glass rendering invisible on light backgrounds.
  • Fixed the format picker vanishing when a row is selected. Clicking a row in the file list turned the format picker into a blank white box — the text was rendering white-on-white because it used colours that invert to white on a blue selected row. The label now stays legible in both selected and unselected states.

New Features

  • Two new PDF tools, in a redesigned sidebar. Picmal's tools now live down the side, grouped into Media (Convert, Compress) and PDF (Combine PDFs, Images to PDF), so there's room to grow beyond converting and compressing.
  • Combine PDFs. Drop in several PDFs, drag to reorder them, and merge everything into one document. Name the output file in PDF Options, or leave it blank for an automatic name. The combined PDF is saved next to the first file.
  • Images to PDF. Turn a batch of images into a single PDF, one image per page. Drag to set the page order, pick a page size (fit to image, A4, Letter or a custom size in mm), set the image quality, add an optional password, and name the output file.
  • Both PDF tools also work from the Finder right-click menu, the Shortcuts app, and the command line (`picmal-cli combine` and `picmal-cli images-to-pdf`). You get a notification when the PDF is ready, just like Convert and Compress.
  • Custom metadata control. On top of strip-all, keep-essential and keep-all, a new Custom mode lets you choose exactly which categories to keep — location (GPS), camera & exposure, date & time, copyright & author, colour profile, orientation, serial & owner IDs, and the embedded thumbnail — each on its own. The command line gains matching `--keep` and `--strip` flags.

Improvements

  • A fresh coat of Liquid Glass. The bottom bar, the clipboard overlay, and the licence banner now use macOS's Liquid Glass look, so they sit more naturally over whatever's behind them.
  • Combining PDFs now reports a clear error if a page can't be read, instead of quietly leaving it out of the merged file.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed resizing and compressing in one go producing bloated files. When an image was both resized and compressed — in Compress mode or a watched folder — the resize step quietly undid the optimisation, leaving files much larger than doing the two steps separately. The output is now optimised properly, so combined resize and compress matches a resize-then-optimise pass.
  • Fixed converted photos coming out sideways. Portrait shots from your iPhone (and any photo that relies on a rotation tag) were being flipped to landscape on convert. Picmal now rotates the pixels upright so the output looks exactly like the original. The Orientation setting (Auto-fix / Keep tag) in Settings → Images now does what it says, and the command line rotates correctly too.
  • Fixed conversions and compressions that could freeze or stall. A quick one-off job (like a single photo) could hang right as it finished, and big batches could get stuck partway. The heavy PDF, SVG, and image work now runs to the side, so the app stays responsive and files keep moving.
  • Fixed some audio failing to convert to OGG. Converting to OGG (Vorbis) could fail with an "encoder setup failed" error, most often on lower-sample-rate files like 22 kHz MP3s. Picmal now sets the Vorbis quality directly instead of a target bitrate, which the encoder handles reliably, so these conversions go through.
  • Fixed a crash when removing files with the Delete key. Deleting selected rows from the keyboard while the list was updating could bring the app down. Deletions now wait for the list to settle, the same way the right-click Remove already did.

• Fixed a crash that could strike mid-run when the file list was busy reshuffling itself. Rows now hold their place while they process and only move when a file finishes or you change its priority, so a big batch stays steady instead of jumping around.
  • Fixed a rare crash inside Picmal's own crash-reporting, where tidying up an error report could itself bring the app down instead of just quietly logging it.
  • Updated the crash-reporting library and brought the command line tool in line with the app, so both report problems the same way under the hood.
  • Fixed the video speed control. Custom speed now takes a clear multiplier (type 5 for 5×, up to 8×) instead of a confusing percentage, and the Delete key edits the field properly instead of removing the file from the list.

• Compress images to a target file size. Pick "Max File Size" in the resize settings, type a size (100 KB, 2 MB, whatever you need), and Picmal scales each image down just enough to fit. Works in Convert, Compress, watched folders, and the command line (`picmal-cli convert -i photo.jpg -f jpg --resize 100kB`).
  • Better image compression all round. JPEGs come out sharper (optimised Huffman coding, a higher-precision transform, and full colour kept at the top quality settings), AVIF and JPEG XL are tighter, GIF frame optimisation is smarter, and for still images WebP keeps whichever of two encodings is smaller.
  • Picmal never hands you a file bigger than the original when compressing. If a pass wouldn't save space, your original is kept untouched — now everywhere, including when you compress straight after converting.
  • Add your own copyright to every image. Fill in the new Copyright & ownership fields in Settings (copyright notice, artist, credit, contact) and Picmal stamps them into each exported photo across EXIF, IPTC, and XMP. It works even when you're stripping metadata: the camera and location data come off, your copyright stays on. You only type it once — it's saved and reused on every export, with a switch to turn it on or off without clearing the fields. There are matching flags for the command line too (`picmal-cli convert -i photo.jpg -f jpg --copyright "(c) 2026 You" --artist "Your Name"`).
  • Check what actually made it into a file. The ⓘ button on a finished file now has an Original / Result switch and opens on Result, so you can see at a glance that your copyright landed and the camera and location data came off. It turns up even when the original had no metadata, so copyright you added is easy to confirm too.
  • The metadata setting now spells out the trade-off as you pick it. Choose "Strip all" and it tells you straight: smallest files, but the original's camera, date, and copyright info go with them.
  • Fixed Compress ignoring the Metadata setting. It used to strip everything no matter what, so "Keep essential" and "Keep all" did nothing when compressing. Now it keeps exactly what you pick (and adds your copyright), and photos keep their orientation.
  • Fixed the metadata popover that collapsed to a single line — it now sizes itself to the metadata and scrolls when there's a lot. It also shows the latest output every time, instead of occasionally serving up a stale earlier reading.

• Faster video conversion and compression, especially on powerful Macs with lots of cores. Picmal now runs a few video encodes side by side instead of starving them all, gives each one a proper share of the CPU, and AV1 output is 20–40× quicker. Watched-folder and clipboard jobs run quietly in the background so they don't slow down whatever you're doing.
  • The Finder right-click Convert and Compress options now run reliably even when Picmal is closed. They process quietly in the background without pulling focus from Finder, with a notification showing what Picmal is working on and the progress as it goes (so a long file doesn't look stuck), honour your "Save to subfolder" setting, and let you know when a selection has nothing Picmal can convert instead of just flashing open and closing. The Services menu items are now grouped together as "Picmal — Add Files", "Picmal — Convert" and "Picmal — Compress".

• Two new audio formats you can convert to and compress: EAC3 (Dolby Digital Plus) and MKA (Matroska audio).
  • Open more audio files to convert from: Monkey's Audio (APE), Musepack (MPC), TAK, DSD (DSF), Shorten (SHN), AMR and GSM. These are read-only, so you can convert them to any other format but Picmal won't write them back out.
  • A new video format you can convert to and compress: 3G2 (3GPP2 mobile video).
  • Open more video files to convert from: RealMedia (RM, RMVB), Bink (BIK), FLIC animation (FLI, FLC), Nullsoft Streaming Video (NSV) and Dahua CCTV (DAV). These are read-only, so you can convert them to any other format but Picmal won't write them back out.
  • Fixed reopening Picmal sometimes bringing up the Settings window instead of the main window.
  • Fixed conversions started from the Finder right-click menu stalling when Picmal launched in the background. They now run straight away, and a licence check no longer fires twice on launch.

• Big and animated WebPs convert and compress much faster again, and large animated WebPs no longer fail with an out-of-memory error or stall for minutes. A single large file now uses all your CPU cores and gets the memory it needs, while big batches still run many files side by side.
  • A big batch of new image formats you can convert to: HDR (Radiance), DPX and Cineon (film), FITS (astronomy), Photoshop Large (PSB), Pyramid TIFF, PAM, PFM, PHM, MIFF, VIPS, AVS, multi-page PCX (DCX), MATLAB (MAT), VICAR, Animated PNG (APNG), MNG, JNG, Farbfeld, Sun Raster, Palm Pixmap and Database, Wireless Bitmap (WBMP), Group 3 FAX, Sixel, Khoros VIFF and WordPerfect Graphics (WPG).
  • Open many more camera RAW files: Olympus (ORF), Panasonic (RW2), Pentax (PEF), Samsung (SRW), newer Canon (CR3, CRW), Hasselblad (3FR, FFF), Phase One (IIQ), Sigma (X3F), Leica (RWL), Sony (SR2, SRF), Kodak (DCR, KDC, K25), Epson (ERF), Mamiya (MEF), Minolta (MRW, MDC) and Nikon (NRW) — with your camera metadata kept.
  • Open GIMP (XCF), OpenRaster (ORA), DICOM, Kodak Photo CD and Ultra HDR files too.
  • The output format picker is now grouped (Common, Raster, RAW, Scientific, Legacy) and searchable, so the longer list stays easy to navigate. All the new formats are available in the Shortcuts app as well.
  • The Finder right-click "Convert with Picmal" and "Compress with Picmal" options now run the conversion or compression straight away, instead of just adding the files to the window. A new "Add to Picmal" option keeps the old behaviour for when you just want to drop files in without processing them.

• Fixed audio and video conversion in the `picmal-cli` command line tool. It used to hang forever when run directly in a Terminal.
  • Fixed HEVC (H.265) video conversion failing on Macs with lots of CPU cores (like the iMac Pro and Mac Pro). The software encoder was asking for more threads than it allows and refused to start.
  • When the hardware video encoder chokes on a tricky clip (for example 10-bit footage with a timecode track), Picmal now automatically retries in software instead of giving up, so the conversion still finishes.
  • Fixed a crash when a scheduled batch started while you had files selected in the list.

• Fixed batch conversions failing with a temporary-file error when "Save to subfolder" was on. The output subfolder is now created up front, and if a destination really can't be written to, only those files are marked failed instead of crashing the whole batch.
  • Fixed the Finder right-click "Convert with Picmal" and "Compress with Picmal" options doing nothing. The window now comes to the front and the files land in the list, whether Picmal was closed, already running, or hidden in the menu bar.
  • Zoom in and out in the Before/After window to inspect fine compression detail. Pinch on the trackpad, use the new + / − / 100% controls in the corner, or press ⌘+, ⌘−, ⌘0. Drag to pan while zoomed; the slider handle still moves the divider at any zoom level. Double-click to reset.
  • Picmal now has a command line tool. Convert and compress images, audio, and video straight from the Terminal, using the same engines as the app. Run `picmal-cli convert -i photo.heic -f jpg`, `picmal-cli compress -i big.png --quality 70`, or `picmal-cli watch` to monitor a folder. It supports presets, resizing, metadata stripping, colour space and DPI options, and watermarks, and outputs NDJSON when you pipe it into other tools. It uses your existing Picmal licence.

• Embed album art into audio automatically. Turn on "Embed cover art from the source folder" in Settings → Audio and Picmal looks for a cover image (cover.jpg, folder.jpg, front.jpg — editable) next to each track and adds it to MP3, M4A, ALAC and FLAC output. "Skip files that already have artwork" keeps any existing cover instead of replacing it.
  • See how much space you saved after compressing. When a batch finishes, the bottom bar and the completion notification show the total freed space with a playful comparison, like "Freed up 9.66 GB · about a 4K movie 🎬".
  • Schedule a batch for later. Tap the clock button next to Convert (or Compress) to pick a start time, handy for running big jobs overnight. The bottom bar shows what's queued, you get a notification when it finishes, and schedules survive quitting and reopening Picmal.
  • Converting RAW photos (NEF, CR2, ARW, RAF, DNG) now keeps your camera metadata. With "Keep all metadata" the output JPEG carries the make, model, lens, exposure, date and GPS. "Keep essential" keeps the basics while dropping location and serial numbers. The metadata indicator now reads RAW files too, so it no longer shows them as empty.

• See an estimate of a video's compressed size before you run it, so you know roughly how much space you'll save.
  • Set a priority on any file. Right-click and pick High, Normal or Low, and high-priority files get processed first, even mid-batch.
  • Pause and resume a running batch. Pause now stops files mid-conversion too, not just the ones still waiting.
  • Right-click any file to show it in Finder, set its priority, or remove it from the list. (The old "File" column is gone, since Show in Finder now lives in the menu.)
  • ALAC (Apple Lossless) conversions are now truly lossless. Converting FLAC to ALAC used to produce a smaller, lossy AAC file by mistake.
  • Fixed Adobe RGB conversions failing on macOS 26 with an "UnrecognizedColorspace" error. Picmal now resolves ICC profiles across macOS versions and skips colour conversion cleanly when a profile is genuinely missing, instead of failing the whole batch.
  • Old FLV videos with mono Speex audio now convert instead of failing at the end with an encoder error.
  • Big batches no longer stall on the last file or two. If an image encoder gets stuck, Picmal kills it and retries within about 15 seconds.
  • The file list scrolls smoothly while processing, and the "X of Y files compressed" count no longer freezes just short of the total.
  • PDF compression never hands you a file bigger than the original. If it wouldn't save space, Picmal keeps your original.
  • Cancelling a batch now stops quickly and tidies up, so interrupted files go back to "Waiting" instead of looking stuck.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Watermarks were sometimes skipped on a few files in a batch. Fixed: every image gets one now.
  • Watermarks can scale to a percentage of each image's height, so one preset looks right on photos of any size. Turn on "Scale to image" in the watermark editor and drag the slider.
  • "Keep all metadata" was quietly dropping some tags. It really keeps everything now.
  • PDF to JPG/PNG no longer dumps huge files on you. Pick the rasterisation DPI in Settings → Images (72, 150, 300 or 600). Default is 150.
  • Drag-and-drop used to silently cap at 100 files. You can now drop up to 10,000 at once and they all land in the list.
  • Audio conversions now let you pick a bit depth (16, 24 or 32 bit) on top of the sample rate. The new "CD quality" preset is 16 bit + 44.1 kHz FLAC.
  • Picking Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Rec. 709 or Rec. 2020 as the output colour space used to fail outright; only sRGB worked. Fixed.
• You can now convert MOD camcorder videos (JVC, Canon, Panasonic) to MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, MPG, and GIF.
• Fixed a crash on Intel Macs.

• Save your own compression presets for images, audio, and video. Tweak the settings you like, hit "Save as preset", name it, and it shows up next to the built-in ones.
  • ALAC (Apple Lossless) is now an output format. Convert FLAC, WAV, or AIFF to a lossless `.m4a` that imports straight into Apple Music.

• Replaced the notch progress overlay with standard macOS notifications. Watched-folder activity now shows up as native banners (queued, per-file progress, and final result) that collapse into a single entry in Notification Center instead of a floating panel.

• Fixed larger WebP files failing to convert to GIF. Animated and high-resolution WebPs now get a 5-minute ceiling instead of being killed at 2, and the error is clearer when a source really is too large or has too many frames.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Menu bar quick controls: open a file picker with ⇧⌘O, and adjust clipboard behaviour inline. On Copy mode (Compress / Convert / Compress & Convert), Target Format, and Auto-Copy Result now sit under the Optimize Clipboard toggle and stay in sync with Settings.
  • Fixed an infinite loop where Auto-Copy reprocessed the file Picmal had just put on the clipboard, stacking overlay entries and re-running compression.
  • Fixed `.jpeg` files producing a sibling `.jpg` instead of overwriting (or keeping the source extension) on both compress and convert. Same-format operations now keep the input's extension, so `.jpeg`, `.tif`, and similar aliases stay consistent.
• Rebuilt the Settings window from scratch for a cleaner, more native feel.

• Rename output files from their EXIF metadata with a filename pattern. Tokens: {original}, {date}, {datetime}, {year}, {month}, {day}, {camera}, {iso}.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Polished the watermark section and fixed some visual glitches.
  • Faster image conversion.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Burn-in subtitles for video. Attach an SRT or VTT file to any video from the new film icon next to its name, and the text is burned into the output. Style it in Settings → Video (size, colour, top/center/bottom).
  • Per-video playback speed. The same film icon lets you pick 0.25×, 0.5×, 2×, 4× or a custom percentage (10–800%). Audio keeps its natural pitch. "Apply speed to all videos" copies it across the batch.
  • Image and video watermarks. Add a logo or PNG overlay to any image or video, save multiple presets, and set position (9 anchors), margins, and opacity in Settings → Watermark.
  • Fixed resize settings being ignored when compressing. Max Dimensions, Max Width/Height, and the other modes now apply to compressed images, just like Convert.

• Redesigned the Settings window.
  • Licence activation errors now include guidance and a link to the deactivation docs when a licence is already active on another device.
  • Clipboard optimisation now lets you choose what happens when you copy an image: compress, convert to another format (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF or GIF), or both.

• Fixed conversions hanging forever (stuck at 99% or 0%) when batch-converting lots of files at once.
  • Fixed high CPU use after conversions finish.
  • Overwrite warnings: a warning icon now shows in the convert table when a same-format conversion would overwrite the original, and in the compress bottom bar when the prefix/suffix are empty. The Output settings page shows per-section warnings too.
  • JPEG compression failures now capture error output for diagnostics.
  • Removed the automatic "\_converted" suffix for same-format conversions. Use the prefix/suffix settings instead.

• You can now convert audio to the same format (e.g. FLAC to FLAC) to change the sample rate without switching codec.
  • New sample rate setting in Audio > Custom: resample to 8, 11.025, 16, 22.05, 32, 44.1 (CD), 48 (DVD), 88.2 or 96 kHz.
  • Same-format conversions now add a "\_converted" suffix so they don't overwrite the original.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.
• Fixed MP4 to GIF conversion.

• Picmal now detects corrupted video files (like ones missing the moov atom) and tells you clearly instead of failing without explanation.
  • Faster launch. The app no longer waits on non-essential setup before showing the first screen.
  • Cancelling a conversion is smoother and no longer briefly freezes the UI.
  • Fixed concurrency issues in ServiceHandler, SharedTempFileManager, and FFmpegConverter.
  • Replaced system notifications with a progress overlay that animates from the notch or slides down on other displays.
  • The menu bar icon now shows live progress.
  • Clearer error messages.
  • Other smaller fixes and improvements.

• Fixed JPEG compression silently producing truncated, corrupted files.
  • Fixed high CPU use when idle, caused by aggressive clipboard polling, always-on cache timers, broad UserDefaults observation, and unbatched FSEvents.
  • Watched folders now support per-folder resize settings and a "compress after convert" option.
  • New auto-copy for clipboard optimisation: compressed images go straight back to the clipboard, skipping the Copy button. Off by default.
  • Video compression now lets you change the container (MOV to MP4, MKV, WebM, AVI) and handles codec compatibility for you.

• Before / After preview. Click the eye icon on any processed file to compare the original and the output with a slider.
  • Video compression now has a wider CRF range (0–51) for finer control, plus a frame rate setting to drop fps (say 60 to 30) and shrink files further.

• Picmal remembers the last output format you picked for each input type, so dropping a new file reuses your choice.
  • The clipboard overlay now disappears after a timeout (5 seconds by default) and stays out of screenshots.

• Better WebP to GIF conversion. Animated WebPs keep all their frames, and static ones convert without errors.
  • New clipboard image optimisation. Images you copy get compressed automatically, and a small overlay lets you grab the optimised version.
  • Set the DPI metadata on output images (72, 96, 144, 150, 300, 600 or custom) for print and display work. It just sets the tag, no resizing.

• Minor fixes.
  • Better licence handling.

• New settings for orientation and metadata, with three modes: strip all, keep essential (orientation, colour profile, copyright), or keep everything.
  • Conversion now works reliably on iCloud Drive, network shares, and read-only locations.
  • HEVC videos with unusual frame rates now convert correctly to MOV and play in QuickTime.
  • Other minor improvements.

• You can now drop files and folders straight into the menu tray.
  • Fixed dragging files onto the dock icon not working.
  • A few small fixes under the hood.

• Fixed the app freezing on complex or corrupted files.
  • Better Sentry error handling.
  • Other minor fixes.
• Added Sentry to catch crashes and errors.

• Better PNG and SVG compression quality.
  • Fixed some crashes on macOS 14, especially for new users.
  • Other minor fixes.

• Clearer error messages when switching between Compress and Convert.
  • The app now starts in the background when launched at login with "Keep in Menu Bar" enabled.
  • Better image compression.
  • Fixed video compression not reducing file sizes, and improved encoding speed.

• Added watched folders with hot folder monitoring.
  • You can now use Picmal from the Shortcuts app.
  • Picmal can run in the background when you log in.
  • Compress on output now works for images, audio, and video.

• Files now stick around when you switch between the Convert and Compress tabs.
  • You can now drag and drop files onto the dock icon.
  • Fixed SVG compression failing on some CSS classes it couldn't read.
  • Added HIF support (Canon HEIF).
  • Fixed a DNG/RAW rotation issue.

• Presets for audio and video conversion.
  • You can now convert HEIC to WebP.
  • Strip metadata from audio, video, and image files.
  • Output files now show the settings used.
  • Rewrote parts of the code for better stability.
  • Reorganised the Preferences menu so it's easier to navigate.
  • Fixed unusable files from MKV to MP4 conversions with certain codecs.

• PDFs come out clearer and sharper.
  • Open files from the menu with File > Open, or press Command O.
  • Picmal now understands folders. Drop one in and it gathers everything inside, including subfolders.
  • New Finder right-click options to convert or compress images with Picmal.

• Color space conversion: convert images to sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Rec. 709 or Rec. 2020, with the right ICC profile embedded.
  • Check a converted image's color space from a new clickable icon in the Size column.
  • Fixed FLAC to AAC conversion in optimised Advanced mode.

• Color space conversion: convert images to sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Rec. 709 or Rec. 2020, with the right ICC profile embedded.
  • Check a converted image's color space from a new clickable icon in the Size column.
  • Fixed FLAC to AAC conversion in optimised Advanced mode.

• You can now convert EPS to SVG.
  • You can now convert AI to SVG.

• You can now convert EPS to SVG.
  • You can now convert AI to SVG.

• Color space conversion: convert images to sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Rec. 709 or Rec. 2020, with the right ICC profile embedded.
  • Check a converted image's color space from a new clickable icon in the Size column.
  • Fixed FLAC to AAC conversion in optimised Advanced mode.

• You can now convert EPS to SVG.
  • You can now convert AI to SVG.

• You can now convert EPS to SVG.
  • You can now convert AI to SVG.
• Added a banner when no licence is active, so it's clear Picmal needs one to run.

• Audio and video now show conversion speed and an estimated time remaining.
  • Video conversions are much faster and use less memory, especially for long files. Instant conversion (no re-encoding) now works for 50+ format combinations, including WebM, MKV, MP4, FLV, and 3GP.
  • VideoToolbox H.264 hardware encoding now covers 12+ video formats on Apple Silicon, making FLV, WMV, MPEG, 3GP, WTV, F4V and MXF 10–50× faster.
  • Fixed WebM codec handling in Advanced mode (it now enforces VP8/VP9/AV1 properly).
  • Fixed the metadata, progress, and Show in Finder buttons being unclickable during conversion.
  • PDF compression is faster and more accurate.

• Fixed multi-select for audio and video files. The format dropdown now populates correctly when you select media files with the checkbox.
  • Fixed wrong savings percentages when converting between formats.

• Fixed the non-clickable checkbox in Advanced mode.
  • Added Advanced mode to both Convert and Compress.
  • The bottom tab bar now truncates text when there's too much of it.
  • Fixed several PDF compression errors.
